verdict.rationale: ROS 2's core architecture—standard message packages, topics/services/actions interfaces, and multi-language client libraries—is exactly the mechanism that lets drivers for different sensors/actuators publish/subscribe to the same standardized interface, enabling swap-in-place hardware. However, the evidence pack never explicitly documents a 'hardware abstraction layer' concept, driver ecosystem practices, or a concrete example of swapping a sensor/actuator without app changes. Missing for 10: explicit hardware-abstraction/driver-interface documentation, named sensor/actuator driver packages demonstrating swap-ability, and independent hands-on confirmation that application code needs no changes when hardware is swapped.
